To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an HIV-1-based vector system that is independent of the Rev-RRE nuclear export pathway.
we have developed a Rev-independent HIV-1 gene delivery system for targeting the HIV-1 nucleo-cytoplasmic RNA trafficking pathway for inhibiting virus replication.
we have created a Rev-free HIV- 1-based packaging system that can be used to target HIV-1 Rev for inhibition of viral gene expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of HIV-based gene delivery systems.
the design of a Rev-free packaging system that can be used to deliver a dominant negative Rev transgene to T-cells for inhibiting HIV-1 infection and replication.
developing a gene delivery system that can be used to target HIV-1 Rev-RRE-CRM1 nucleocytoplamic RNA transport pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HIV-1 based packaging system containing MPMV CTEs can be used to produce Rev-free vector stocks that can be used to target the Rev-RRE- Crm1 nucleocytoplamic RNA transport pathway for the inhibition of HIV replication.

the use of the MPMV RNA transport elements for the creation of Rev-independent packaging systems can provide a novel attribute to HIV-1 based vectors for targeting the Rev/RRE/Crm-1 pathway for the inhibition of HIV replication.
the use of RNA elements from different viruses in the HIV-1 gene delivery system can provide novel attributes such as improved safety and Rev-independence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a Rev-free HIV- 1-based gene delivery system by using the constitutive transport element (CTEs) from Mason-Pfiser monkey virus (MPMV) to target the Rev-RRE-crm1 nucleocyoplasmic RNA transport path way in order to inhibit HIV replication in T-lymphocyte cells.
the use of MPMV RNA transport elements in the context of a Rev-free HIV- 1 gene delivery system can provide an improved safety profile and a high-titered vector stock.
the use of multiple copies of MPMVs CTE can provide a Rev-free packaging system for HIV-1-based lentiviral gene transfer systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Rev-free gene delivery system is useful for inhibiting HIV-1 replication.
we have developed a Rev-independent packaging system for gene delivery.
the use of RNA export elements from other viruses can provide novel features to an HIV-1 gene therapy system such as improved safety.
